suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-18 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited review reported significant psychiatric comorbidity and symptom overlap between chronic fatigue syndrome and depressive and other psychiatric disorders without establishing individual causation or direction. Require independently established chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS/ME) and a separately established depressive disorder; the cited review reported substantial comorbidity and symptom overlap between chronic fatigue syndrome and depressive and other psychiatric disorders without establishing onset order, direction, or individual causation. Preserve other medical illness, sleep disorders, substance use, medications, endocrine disease, anemia, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from fatigue, post-exertional malaise, or impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that chronic fatigue syndrome caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
